moments.title: She pushed back on her CA friend's fund picks and suggested flexi-caps
moments.summary: A participant describes telling a close friend who is a CA and an MBA to look at particular flexi-caps rather than the ones being suggested — funds her husband had evaluated — and to check the rates of return on them.
moments.evidence: You might want to look at these flexi-caps, not the ones that you are suggesting.

moments.title: Confident she can see herself doing well with the family's money
moments.summary: She says the course has made her more confident that in a few years she will be doing really well with the money she and her family have, and describes it as an energetic shift.
moments.evidence: it's just making me more confident that I can see myself in a few years doing really well with the money we have for myself and my family.

moments.title: Cross-learning from the group, not just from the instructor
moments.summary: A participant says her group asked a lot of questions and there was real back-and-forth, so there was learning from the instructor — named in the room as Hiral — but also from each other, which made the session more informative and enjoyable.
moments.evidence: So there was learning from the instructor, Hiral, but there's also learning from each other and that makes it a much more informative and enjoyable session.

moments.title: The games showed them they don't have to play the way they usually do
moments.summary: Asked for the most fun part, several participants immediately say the games, and one adds that the games make you see how you play and give you the chance to change — that she does not need to use that kind of mindset anymore.
moments.evidence: I don't need to play like how I typically do. I don't need to use that kind of mindset anymore.
